# Code of conduct

Be decent to people. Assume the person on the other end is trying to make something work, usually late at night, usually after several hours of a plug-in not loading.

Specifically:

- Criticize the work, not the person. "This recipe does X, which will break Y" is useful. "This is obviously wrong" is not.
- Report what you observed, not what you assume. A compatibility claim without evidence costs everyone else time.
- Do not pressure anyone into testing something on an environment holding their licences. Losing an activation is a real cost to a real person.
- No harassment, personal attacks, or unwelcome attention of any kind.
- Do not post other people's licence keys, account data, or personal information, including your own by accident.

## If something goes wrong

Report it to the maintainer privately by email. Reports are handled as discreetly as circumstances allow. Unacceptable behaviour can result in comments being removed, a pull request being closed, or a contributor being blocked.

The maintainer holds themselves to the same standard, and can be told when they fall short of it.
